tax.text: Irwin said wealthy people and corporations should pay more in taxes.
tax.quote: Irwin and Epsinosa both said rich people and corporation should pay more in taxes.

trade.text: Irwin said President Trump’s tariffs were arbitrary, uninformed and harmful to the economy.
trade.quote: She said his tariffs were arbitrary, uninformed and harmful to the economy

housing.text: Irwin said she would reduce regulatory burdens on housing development to help address living costs.
housing.quote: reducing regulatory burdens on housing development

immigration.text: Irwin said she supports strong borders while opposing ICE’s budget, alleged racial profiling and untrained agents.
immigration.quote: Democrats Jacqui Irwin and Sonia Kacker both said they support “strong borders,” but both criticized ICE as well.

guns.text: Irwin authored a California bill establishing a pilot project involving restrictions on firearm possession.
guns.quote: AB 1344 by Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin (D-Thousand Oaks)– Restrictions on firearm possession: pilot project.

abortion.text: Irwin authored AB 2531 to provide veterans access to abortion care at no or reduced cost.
abortion.quote: California’s veteran population has access to receiving abortion care in this state at no cost or reduced cost.

cannabis.text: Has a mixed cannabis record, including sponsoring restrictive measures, opposing cannabis cafes and advancing a bill extending cannabis compassion programs.
cannabis.quote: Mixed voting record. Sponsored failed bills to ban cannabis billboards and impose restrictive labeling requirements on cannabis products; voted against cannabis cafes; skipped votes on employment rights, medical access. To her credit, she did move AB 2555, a bill to extend cannabis compassion programs

health.text: Irwin said she would fight to reverse cuts to federal healthcare programs and insurance subsidies.
health.quote: And Irwin said Congress should “fight to reverse the Trump cuts” to federal health care programs and insurance subsidies.

energy.text: Irwin highlighted her role in reauthorizing California’s cap-and-trade program to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions.
energy.quote: Irwin, who represents the eastern half of Ventura County in the State Assembly, touted her role in reauthorizing the state’s cap and trade program, a market-based policy that allows companies to trade emission credits to reduce overall greenhouse emissions.

trade.text: Said tariffs should be implemented more precisely and with better targeting.
trade.quote: But the candidate said the implementation of tariffs could have been more precise and targeted.

debt.text: Said the federal deficit is out of control and mentioned cutting fraud, waste and abuse from the budget.
debt.quote: Koslow, Kacker and Gallucci all mentioned cutting “fraud, waste and abuse” from the budget

housing.text: He supports incentivizing homebuilding and streamlining regulations that delay and raise construction costs.
housing.quote: Incentivize homebuilding near jobs and transit; streamline federal regulations that delay and inflate construction costs.

immigration.text: He supports funding the mass removal of criminal illegal aliens while also streamlining work permits in fields with labor shortages.
immigration.quote: Streamline work permitting in fields with labor shortages so employers can fill needed jobs.

energy.text: He wants to expand domestic energy production and streamline permits to lower utility bills.
energy.quote: Unleash American energy to lower utility bills; streamline permits for domestic production and grid upgrades.
